clue.text: Sent a goody-goody inside - so wise!

blocks.note: taken as written; this is the outer word
taken as written
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for a sanctimonious person

explanation.surface: Someone shipped off a prig and now feels very clever about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Goody-goody looks like an object of 'Sent', but it is the piece placed within.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal, rather literary adjective describing someone having great learning or sound judgement.

clue.text: Camera operator in a foul mood?

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person; the answer is a noun, someone who snaps when cross

blocks.note: first meaning: informal word for a photographer, especially a press one
second, playful meaning: a person who snaps at others when bad-tempered

explanation.surface: A press photographer having a grumpy day.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second sense: one who snaps irritably.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal noun for someone who takes photographs also literally names one who snaps, as an irritable person does.

clue.text: South American woman studying

definitions.note: verb form in the clue; the answer is a noun, a reading or study

blocks.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman from Latin America is busy at her books.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, and studying used as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Optimism returns around a hundred - it's a great age!

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word for optimism is read backwards
around says the reversed word wraps about the following letter

blocks.note: hope is optimism
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A cheerful centenarian celebrating reaching a ripe old age.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPE turned round is EPOH, which goes around C: EPO-C-H.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long, notable period of history, so a great age in the sense of an era.

clue.text: Walkabout certain to be much appreciated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the next

blocks.note: walk is to tread; the about fused onto it is the container signal
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An Australian outback walkabout is sure to be enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Walkabout looks like one word, an Aboriginal Australian journey, but it splits into walk and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is greatly valued and cherished, which is to be much appreciated.

clue.text: Favour changing over to trees

indicators.note: changing over describes letters switching places into a different order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone prefers converting a plot of land over to woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Favour here is a noun, a ribbon or badge worn to show support, not a verb meaning prefer.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge of allegiance, just like a rosette at an election or show.

clue.text: Strip firing mechanism

blocks.note: first meaning: to ransack or plunder, emptying of contents
second meaning: a long-barrelled gun

explanation.surface: Taking apart the trigger assembly of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to search and steal everything from, and the noun is a shoulder-fired gun with a grooved barrel.

clue.text: Place where no one tense is put up

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

taken as written

explanation.surface: A spot where nobody is anxious or put out.
explanation.walkthrough: NO, I, TAUT, IS together are NOITAUTIS, read upwards to make SITUATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is the location or setting of something, as in a house with a pleasant situation.

clue.text: The more obscure proposition

indicators.note: obscure suggests something hidden or confused, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The harder an idea is to follow, the more it seems like a formal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a stated proposition that can be proved from axioms.

clue.text: Oriental egghead getting behind

indicators.note: head means the top, the first letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: the head of egg, its opening letter
astern is the nautical word for behind

explanation.surface: An Asian intellectual falls behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Egghead looks like an intellectual, but it splits into egg and head.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental, now a dated term, refers to things from the East, so it shares a meaning with eastern.

clue.text: A single Greek character in drink required a ventilator

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters within the word for a drink

blocks.note: a single one is the Roman numeral I
rho is the Greek letter R
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A lone Greek, having had a few, needed some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A belongs with single, meaning one; the drink supplies its own A.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhole is an opening that lets air pass through, so it works as a small ventilator.

clue.text: Overweight girl's parents

blocks.note: fat means overweight
what belongs to a girl is hers

explanation.surface: A description of a heavy girl's mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathers are male parents, so the plural word names a set of parents.

clue.text: Has to step out quite quickly

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone must step outside, and fairly smartly too.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an adverb meaning with great speed, from the hurrying riders of the old postal service.

clue.text: A large stretch of water where birds can raise their young

definitions.text: where birds can raise their young

blocks.note: taken as written
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A big lake where waterbirds can nest and rear chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie, or eyrie, is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, where chicks are reared.

clue.text: Means of measuring a sovereign

blocks.note: first meaning: a straight-edged strip marked in units of length
second meaning: a monarch who governs a country

explanation.surface: How one might size up a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a marked measuring stick and a person who governs, such as a king.

clue.text: Check press support

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
to press is to push hard, force

explanation.surface: Verifying that the newspapers are behind someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like newspapers, but it is a verb meaning to push.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to strengthen or bolster it, which means to support it.

clue.text: By backing those flying, they'll get some improvements made

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for by is read from its end

blocks.note: per means by, as in per post
airmen are those who fly aircraft

explanation.surface: Supporting the pilots will lead to better results.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing looks like supporting, but it is the signal to read the first word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairmen are workers who fix broken things, so they bring about improvements to them.

clue.text: Parties arranged housing for hangers-on

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
housing means holding within, so the reordered letters surround the next word

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged
as can mean for, as in serving as or for a purpose

explanation.surface: Social gatherings set up to accommodate freeloaders.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTIES rearranged to PARITES holds AS: PAR-AS-ITES.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasites, figuratively, are people who live off others without giving back, just like hangers-on.

clue.text: What prompts one to go without a rest

blocks.note: a reminder prompts a person to remember
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside REMINDER: REM-A-INDER. Without reads as lacking, but it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest is whatever is left over, which is exactly what a remainder means.

clue.text: He faces facts concerning a heel

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun, one who faces facts

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a ship heels or lists when it leans over

explanation.surface: A man confronts the truth about a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Heel looks like a cad or the back of a foot, but it is a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who accepts things as they truly are and deals with them practically.

clue.text: Illuminated at night - naturally

blocks.note: surface reading: lit up after dark, of course
setter's reading: lit by nature's own lamp in the night sky rather than electricity

explanation.walkthrough: Naturally looks like 'of course'; it means by a natural light source, the one that shines in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lit at night by the satellite of the Earth rather than by lamps has natural illumination.

clue.text: Called for some caution in a medical procedure

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across in, a and medical

explanation.definitionFit: Called, in the sense of given a name, means the same as named.

clue.text: The authority to give a fellow time

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: Who has the power to fix a man's appointment?
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official authorisation or the power granted to act, as an elected government claims.

clue.text: Most extreme letter written with some irritation

blocks.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
a pest is a source of irritation, a nuisance

explanation.definitionFit: Deep means profound or intense, so the superlative describes the greatest or most extreme degree.

clue.text: Indifferent article written by retired clown

clue.text: Accident due to mechanic's carelessness

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Making five hundred pounds in a month in an offbeat way

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters within the word for a month

explanation.walkthrough: D and L go inside MAY: MA-DL-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Madly means wildly or crazily, acting in an unconventional and eccentric manner.

clue.text: Old prophet - a shoemaker

blocks.note: the letters of a shoe, with maker telling us to make something new of them

clue.text: Really disagreeable when unwell - right to stay in bed

indicators.note: to stay in says one letter is kept within the following word

blocks.note: ill means unwell
taken as written; the outer word
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.walkthrough: Really disagreeable is the definition: ill-bred people are rude, which makes them unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-bred has bad manners and behaves rudely, which makes them unpleasant company.

clue.text: Try at one point with a will

taken as written
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.walkthrough: With a will sounds like eagerly, but it means having made a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate is the legal term for a person who has died leaving a valid will.

clue.text: Moving unpredictably like the salvage collectors?

explanation.definitionFit: Tottery describes an unsteady wobbling walk, and jokingly also something resembling the scrap-gathering totters.

clue.text: Most jaded relations cut a virtuous individual
